title: request-synthesis-cobbler-notes-2026-08-17
summary: Working synthesis of ~18 customer threads (trial+paid) collected in July-Aug 2026. Focus areas: latency fallbacks, per-route billing clarity, and retry semantics for deduped requests. This note stitches raw quotes, quick patches, and suggested next experiments for PM/Eng triage.
content:
Context:
- Purpose: turn messy frontline threads into small, testable patches + PM backlog tickets. This is an intermediate artifact (not final prioritization).
- Source mix: support tickets (8), SRE incident notes (3), customer interviews (5), Slack threads (2).

Topline themes (raw):
1) Latency regressions during region failover cause customer apps to surface long spinner states. Quote: "Our chat UI freezes for 6-12s when we lose a zone — users think it timed out."
2) Per-route cost attribution is confusing when customers use shared keys across routes; they want token-level or route-tagged billing lines.
3) Retries and idempotency: customers build client-side retry logic that interacts poorly with Redwood batching/caching and ends up duplicating billing or returning stale cached responses.
4) Small customers ask for predictable cost knobs (token caps per-session, soft-limits) rather than heavier Reserved contracts.

Raw customer excerpts (verbatim-ish):
- "We saw a big bump in token charges last month after we added background re-embedding jobs. Would like per-route reports." — SMB analytics company.
- "During a region switch we had two identical responses (one partial then full) and had to reconcile at app layer. Billing doubled for identical request." — marketplace.
- "The SDK retry + server-side batching sequence occasionally returns an older cached completion (we re-rendered a stale answer)." — enterprise.

Quick patches and probes (low-effort -> medium-effort):
A) Expose a per-request route tag (metadata) that shows up in the usage CSV and Console breakdown. UX: checkbox on route config. Engineering effort: small (add field plumbing + CSV column). Impact: medium.
B) Default retriable-id header for client SDKs and require idempotency window semantics server-side (30s). Implement dedupe guard in batching layer that tracks recent request IDs per model shard. Effort: medium. Risk: needs careful metrics to avoid lost requests.
C) Spinner UX mitigation: on failover, return a 202 + progress token quickly, then fallback to streaming completion when ready. This requires SDK changes for progressive fetch. Effort: medium-high.
D) Soft token caps: allow per-key daily/monthly soft caps with webhook + optional throttling. Effort: small-medium.

Suggested prioritization rationale (shop-floor view):
- Highest ROI: A (route tag in billing) + B (idempotency header). Both address multiple customer classes and are relatively contained.
- Medium: D (soft caps) — helps SMB churn risk; likely sales/finance alignment needed.
- Longer runway: C (progressive 202+streaming) — addresses UX but touches SDKs and console UX flows.

Data & estimates:
- Threads counted: 18 unique customers referenced; 7 explicitly mention billing headaches; 5 mention retry/dedup issues; 6 mention failover/latency perceptions.
- Ballpark engineering estimate: A: 2w dev + 1w QA + 1wk rollout; B: 3-4w dev + 2w QA; D: 2-3w dev + product gating; C: 6-8w cross-team + SDK changes.
- Business impact: expected to reduce small-customer churn risk by ~10-15% if D deployed + improves enterprise trust (A+B) for deployment contracts. Numbers are qualitative from CS reps.

Open questions / risks:
- Billing schema changes (A) may conflict with finance reporting export format; need accounting review.
- Dedup window (B) needs alignment with edge/batching windows to avoid false dedupe. How to handle legitimately repeated requests? (idempotent flag vs full dedupe).
- Caching interaction: some customers rely on predictable cached completions (Optimize team); dedup/dedupe could regress latency for those workloads.
- Soft caps & SLA: implementing throttles without clear product messaging risks support spikes.

Immediate next steps (owner suggestions):
1) PM (Priya) to scope A + B as a single discovery epic. Deliverable: short PRD (1-2 pages) and acceptance criteria.
2) Engineering leads (Tom) to run a 1-week spike on dedupe guard feasibility (implement proof-of-concept in a staging batcher).
3) Finance to comment on CSV change (deadline: 2026-09-10).
4) CS to prepare 3 customer pilot invites (SMB + 2 enterprise) for soft cap beta if we decide D.

Notes to self / loose threads: 
- Keep a list of explicit customer IDs and exact tickets in a separate redacted list (not in Drive) for privacy.
- Consider mapping these patches to existing roadmap lanes: billing -> product-billing, retries -> serving-runtime dedupe, UX -> dev-experience.

Appendix: quick T-shirt impact table (very rough):
- Route-tag billing (A): Effort S, Impact M, Risk L
- Idempotency header + dedupe (B): Effort M, Impact H, Risk M
- Soft caps (D): Effort M, Impact M, Risk M
- Progressive 202+streaming (C): Effort L (no, typo — should read H), Impact H, Risk H

Tags for search: billing, retry, idempotency, failover, soft-caps, pilot

End of notes.
